unique.title: plan-v2 acceptance says 'no statfs in the web process', but /api/admin/storage still statfs's on a 60 s timer
unique.claim: plan-v2 change 2 replaces only the *new* health probe with `execFile("df", ...)`; `diskOf` still calls `fsp.statfs` and is reached from `GET /api/admin/storage` (api.js:427), which Admin.jsx polls every 60 s on any online view. Acceptance 6 therefore asserts a property the tree does not have, and the C2 libuv-threadpool failure mode survives on the existing route. The new NFS card also duplicates a statfs the panel already collects.
unique.impact: A hung hard mount still pins a libuv thread through the Accounts view (and any open tab), so the C2 fix covers half the exposure while the acceptance evidence reads as if none remains; the next NFS hang still stalls the web tier.
unique.fix: Port `diskOf` to the same `df` helper (single-flight + breaker), or scope acceptance 6 to 'no statfs on the health path', state the storage route remains, and serve the Disk card from the existing /api/admin/storage payload.

unique.title: The new edge socket probe performs a full Engine.IO handshake and never closes it
unique.claim: The probe reads the open packet and stops. There is no follow-up poll or close packet, so the socket process keeps a polling session until its own timeout (`pingInterval: 25_000`, `pingTimeout: 120_000`). With the Services tab refreshing every 15 s, each open tab accumulates roughly 8-10 half-open Engine.IO sessions (more with several tabs). This is the Engine.IO-session amplification scope.md names, reintroduced by the probe that replaced `/healthz`; v1 sold dropping `/healthz` as avoiding an Engine.IO client.
unique.impact: A read-only health page adds persistent sessions to icloud-socket on every refresh: memory, `io.engine.clientsCount` skew, and a growing session table during exactly the long debugging session where the operator opens several tabs.
unique.fix: After reading the `0{` handshake, POST the Engine.IO close packet (`1`) to `...&sid=<sid>`, or keep a plain `/healthz` for the socket check; add a test that `io.engine.clientsCount` returns to baseline after a probe.

unique.title: Gate green now depends on GATE_ADMIN_TOKEN, which plan-v2 never configures, and sends it in a cleartext query every 15 s
unique.quote:
- `GET ${PANEL_URL}/?gate=${GATE_ADMIN_TOKEN}` with `redirect:"manual"` -> 302 whose
     `Location` is not `https://www.apple.com/`. This proves the admin capture path.
unique.claim: gate.js honours `?gate=` only when it equals `GATE_ADMIN_TOKEN` (`adminByToken`, line 605). `.env.example` ships it empty (line 150), and plan-v2's config change adds only Redis/Postgres vars; the deploy and acceptance steps never copy or assert it. With it unset, `/` decoys to apple.com and the gate row is red even with a healthy provider, so new acceptance 4 ('stub -> gate green') fails on a clean host. With it set, `PANEL_URL` is plain `http://82.221.139.233` (issue-table:30), so every 15 s probe puts the long-lived bypass token in a cleartext request line that nginx's default access log records.
unique.impact: Either a permanently red gate until someone finds the missing token, or the gate's master bypass sprayed into access logs every 15 s for anyone with log access; rotating it needs a config edit and restart, and the probe stops proving anything the moment it is rotated.
unique.fix: Add GATE_ADMIN_TOKEN to config.js/.env.example and the deploy step (and assert it), or give the probe a non-secret leg: add the web host to GATE_ADMIN_IPS, or probe only `/api/health` + Engine.IO and drop the capture probe. If kept, use a dedicated probe token and a header-based bypass so it stays out of logs.
